h: Vayetzei Ois 1 · Shabbat Truth, Yaakov's Exile and the Dream of Truth
The Awe of Shabbat and the World of Truth

p: The statement of the Sages, of blessed memory
"The awe of Shabbat is upon him,"
is mentioned with regard to his telling the truth,
that he is afraid to lie on Shabbat.
For this is the root of the holiness of Shabbat:
that the aspect of truth shines forth in it.
For Shabbat is a semblance of the World to Come,
while this world is "the world of falsehood,"
I was in a world of falsehood, etc.;
but now that I am in the world of truth,
And this is the division between Yaakov and Esav:
and so too he was named Esav,
"Here is the falsehood (shav) that I created in My world."
And Yaakov took as his portion
as it says: "Grant truth to Yaakov."

rich.text: — הלוקח פרות ממי שאינו נאמן על המעשרות ושכח לעשרן, ושואלו בשבת, יאכל על פיו. חשכה מוצאי שבת, לא יאכל עד שיעשר. One who bought produce from someone not trusted on tithes and forgot to tithe it may ask him on Shabbat and eat on his word; once Shabbat is over he may not eat until he tithes. The Mishnah gives only the ruling; the words Rav Tzadok quotes, “the awe of Shabbat is upon him,” are the Yerushalmi's reason for it (next note).

h: Yaakov's Exile and the Unwitting Killer

p: And it is stated in the Tanchuma (beginning of this parashah):
goes into exile to the cities of refuge, etc.;
and Yaakov our father went into exile to Charan,
fleeing for his life, and he was afraid, etc.
Once the Holy One, blessed be He, saw him
He revealed Himself to him in a dream."
what does Yaakov's exile have to do
And what is the point of His revealing Himself to him,
the Holy One, blessed be He, in a dream,
that the serpent brought death into the world
and this is the trait of Esav,
"You hated the blood of a man in his body,"
that is, the kelipah of murder.
And Yaakov is a chariot for the letter vav,
which is the letter of truth
at the beginning of Parashas Vayikra).
the corruption of falsehood to such a degree,
לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל חֶטְאוֹ.
before the Holy One, blessed be He, over his sin.
who had already made the blemish of death
and he went out like one who deceives the Mind on High
God, may He be blessed, judged him
as the Sages, of blessed memory, said
that he argued: "I did not know,
and I had never in my life seen a slain person;
שֶׁאֲנִי מַכֵּהוּ בְּאֶבֶן וְהוּא מֵת כּוּלֵּי
that if I struck him with a stone he would die? etc."
And because of this he was sentenced to exile,
to be "a wanderer and a fugitive," etc.

rich.text: — הַהוֹרֵג נֶפֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָה, גּוֹלֶה לְעָרֵי מִקְלָט ... וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ גָּלָה לְחָרָן, בּוֹרֵחַ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, וְנִתְיָרַא שֶׁלֹּא יַהֲרֹג אוֹתוֹ הָרָשָׁע עֵשָׂו אָחִיו. מִכֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּצָרָה גְּדוֹלָה נִגְלָה עָלָיו בַּחֲלוֹם. The unwitting killer goes into exile to the cities of refuge; Yaakov went into exile to Charan, fleeing for his life, afraid that Esav would kill him; seeing him in great distress, God appeared to him in a dream. Rav Tzadok's first “etc.” passes over the list of the six cities; his second passes over the stated object of Yaakov's fear, “that the wicked Esav would kill him.”

h: Yaakov's Fear after Taking the Blessings

p: when he went in to his father,
as is stated in the holy Zohar
that it was then that he said:
from a lying lip, from a deceitful tongue."
And certainly at the time of the deed
he reasoned that according to the law
he was permitted to deviate [from the truth]
and as is stated in Sefer Chassidim
that one is permitted to say
a statement that can be understood two ways.
And as they said regarding Yaakov,
that he said: "I am the one bringing [it],
And he was compelled to this,
so that the serpent would not come out
that because of this he needed
and go into exile to Charan,
that he had made some blemish
in the aspect of truth in this matter,
so much so that because of it he had
to flee for fear of Esav,
since there was found in him as well
which is the camp of Esav.
through the "leaven in the dough" in the heart
And so it seemed to him
that it was like killing unintentionally,
for which he had become liable to exile to Charan.
It is like what is stated (Sanhedrin 97a)
and he deviated there from the truth
and they expelled him from there,
"and do not provoke death among them";
to have erred inadvertently in this,
a trace of the blemish of falsehood,
and thereby had become liable to exile.

h: The Dream That Confirmed His Truth

p: Over this he was deeply embittered,
and his heart cried out to Hashem:
rescue my soul from a lying lip" —
that his soul not be judged
for this as a lying lip.
so that it becomes clear that it was done in truth.
And about this the Midrash said:
"Once the Holy One, blessed be He, saw him
He revealed Himself to him in a dream."
נִתְבָּרֵר לוֹ לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
it became clear to Yaakov our father, peace be upon him,
that he had not blemished the trait of truth at all.
For as is known, it is impossible
for a dream to be without idle matters
yet to Yaakov our father, peace be upon him,
the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared in a dream
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהִנֵּה ה' נִצָּב עָלָיו.
as it says: "And behold, Hashem stood over him."
From this he was confident in himself
that he cleaves to the trait of truth
and had certainly not blemished it at all in this.
And as the Sages, of blessed memory, said
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּא אָחִיךָ בְּמִרְמָה
on the verse "Your brother came with guile":
that Yaakov should take the blessings

rich.text: — רַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא אַשְׁלֵים לֵיהּ כִּיסֵיהּ, אֲזַל אוֹתְבֵיהּ בֵּי קִיבְרֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ. אִתְחֲזִי לֵיהּ בְּחֶלְמֵיהּ: תָּא שְׁקֵיל כִּיסָא דְּמַנַּח אַרֵישָׁא דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא. לִמְחַר אֲמַר לְהוּ ... אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֶלְמָא דְּבֵי שִׁמְשֵׁי לֵית בְּהוּ מַמָּשָׁא. R. Meir would not leave his purse with the innkeeper Kidor, whose name marked him as wicked, and hid it at the grave of the man's father. In a dream the innkeeper was told to take the purse lying at that man's head. When he told them, they said: dreams of bei shimshei have no substance. Rav Tzadok's reading at [5.26]–[5.29], that the dream came from the father's spirit, rests on this detail: the purse was hidden in the father's grave.

rich.text: — דבי שמשי: של ערבי שבתות. לית בהו ממשא: מתוך שאדם במנוחה מהרהר ורואה חלומות, ומתכון היה לדחותו שלא ילך ויטלנו. Bei shimshei means Friday nights; such dreams lack substance because a resting person muses and dreams. Rashi adds that R. Meir meant to put the man off so he would not go and take it.

rich.text: — רבא רמי: כתיב בחלום אדבר בו, וכתיב וחלמות השוא ידברו. לא קשיא: כאן על ידי מלאך, כאן על ידי שד. Rava set the verses against each other: one dream comes through an angel, the other through a demon. Rav Tzadok writes “Berachos, there,” after citing 55a at [4.20]; the contradiction itself is on 55b.

rich.text: — לפי מה שאמרו פרק הרואה דחלום אמתי הוא על ידי מלאך וחלום של שקר הוא על ידי שד, ואם כן זה החלום בודאי לא היה על ידי מלאך להודיע לבנו שיגנוב כיס זה של רבי מאיר, וזה החלום על ידי השד נמי אינו, שהרי אמת היה. The Maharsha's question is exactly as Rav Tzadok reports it. His answer is different: the dream followed the man's own thoughts, since all day he had been plotting how to get R. Meir's money. Rav Tzadok answers instead that the father's spirit counseled him.
